title: Services for turning difficult AI, research, legal, and organizational work into governed systems.
summary: Aloha AI scopes advisory, intelligence, workflow, implementation, and education engagements around the decisions, evidence, ownership, and maintenance a durable system requires.
audience: Organizations that need a clear path from a complex problem to an accountable operating system.
timeline: Most engagements begin with a bounded diagnostic or systems audit before moving into architecture, implementation, or retained support.
fit: The problem crosses functions or disciplines
The work depends on changing evidence
AI is being added without clear ownership or review
A reusable system is more valuable than another one-off deliverable
evidence: Applicable technical, legal, scientific, and institutional authorities
Current policies, roles, and failure cases
assumptions: The organization provides access to representative work and constraints
limitations: Engagements do not replace licensed professional advice
Scope and results depend on access, evidence quality, and organizational participation
